verses.text: Now Moses was keeping the flock of Jethro, his father-in-law, the priest of Midian, and he led the flock to the back of the wilderness, and came to God’s mountain, to Horeb.
Yahweh’s  angel appeared to him in a flame of fire out of the middle of a bush. He looked, and behold, the bush burned with fire, and the bush was not consumed.
Moses said, “I will turn aside now, and see this great sight, why the bush is not burned.”
When Yahweh saw that he turned aside to see, God called to him out of the middle of the bush, and said, “Moses! Moses!” He said, “Here I am.”
He said, “Don’t come close. Take your sandals off of your feet, for the place you are standing on is holy ground.”
Moreover he said, “I am the God of your father, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.” Moses hid his face; for he was afraid to look at God.
Yahweh said, “I have surely seen the affliction of my people who are in Egypt, and have heard their cry because of their taskmasters, for I know their sorrows.

I have come down to deliver them out of the hand of the Egyptians, and to bring them up out of that land to a good and large land, to a land flowing with milk and honey; to the place of the Canaanite, the Hittite, the Amorite, the Perizzite, the Hivite, and the Jebusite.
Now, behold, the cry of the children of Israel has come to me. Moreover I have seen the oppression with which the Egyptians oppress them.
Come now therefore, and I will send you to Pharaoh, that you may bring my people, the children of Israel, out of Egypt.”
Moses said to God, “Who am I, that I should go to Pharaoh, and that I should bring the children of Israel out of Egypt?”
He said, “Certainly I will be with you. This will be the token to you, that I have sent you: when you have brought the people out of Egypt, you shall serve God on this mountain.”
Moses said to God, “Behold, when I come to the children of Israel, and tell them, ‘The God of your fathers has sent me to you;’ and they ask me, ‘What is his name?’ What should I tell them?”
God said to Moses, “I AM WHO I AM,” and he said, “You shall tell the children of Israel this: ‘I AM has sent me to you.’”

God said moreover to Moses, “You shall tell the children of Israel this, ‘Yahweh, the God of your fathers, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, has sent me to you.’ This is my name forever, and this is my memorial to all generations.

Go, and gather the elders of Israel together, and tell them, ‘Yahweh, the God of your fathers, the God of Abraham, of Isaac, and of Jacob, has appeared to me, saying, “I have surely visited you, and seen that which is done to you in Egypt;

and I have said, I will bring you up out of the affliction of Egypt to the land of the Canaanite, the Hittite, the Amorite, the Perizzite, the Hivite, and the Jebusite, to a land flowing with milk and honey.”’

They will listen to your voice, and you shall come, you and the elders of Israel, to the king of Egypt, and you shall tell him, ‘Yahweh, the God of the Hebrews, has met with us. Now please let us go three days’ journey into the wilderness, that we may sacrifice to Yahweh, our God.’
I know that the king of Egypt won’t give you permission to go, no, not by a mighty hand.
I will reach out my hand and strike Egypt with all my wonders which I will do among them, and after that he will let you go.
I will give this people favor in the sight of the Egyptians, and it will happen that when you go, you shall not go empty-handed.

But every woman shall ask of her neighbor, and of her who visits her house, jewels of silver, jewels of gold, and clothing; and you shall put them on your sons, and on your daughters. You shall plunder the Egyptians.”

footnotes.content: Moses, the man raised in Pharaoh's courts, now tends his father-in-law's flock in the wilderness—a world away from power. Forty years of obscurity, and yet the Lord had been shaping him for this very place, this very moment. Sometimes our exile is His preparation.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A bush aflame yet unconsumed—the visible sign of God's presence, burning without destruction. In my long years, I've learned that genuine holiness doesn't consume; it purifies and persists. The Lord's fire is always cleansing, never merely destroying.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Moses turns aside to see—and in that moment of curiosity and obedience, the encounter begins. The Lord often waits for our willingness to step closer, to see what He is doing. Attention itself is a form of worship.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: God calls his name twice—"Moses! Moses!"—with an urgency and intimacy that commands presence. When He calls twice like that, something sacred is about to unfold. We answer "Here I am," and our lives pivot at the hinge.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "Remove your sandals"—the act of stepping onto holy ground barefoot is the oldest gesture of reverence. To stand before the living God, we shed what separates us from the earth He made, surrendering our defenses and meeting Him with nothing between.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob—the Lord anchors His identity in covenant history, showing Moses He has not abandoned His people, even in slavery. And Moses hides his face in fear; true reverence bows us down before the majesty we cannot bear to look upon directly.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "I have surely seen...and have heard...I know their sorrows." The Lord speaks as one who witnesses suffering; He is not distant or indifferent. In my years, I've found that the deepest comfort comes when someone truly sees and knows our pain. The Lord does both with infinite compassion.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: From slavery to a land flowing with milk and honey—the Lord's redemption always moves from bondage to abundance, from death to life. He does not simply free us from something; He frees us *into* something better. Deliverance is never just escape; it is invitation home.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The cry of Israel has come to God—their groaning reached heaven before any prophet proclaimed it. The Lord hears what we dare not speak aloud. Our suffering is not lost in silence; it rises before the throne of grace.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "Come now therefore, and I will send you." The Lord does not ask Moses if he is willing—He calls him to come, already sending. It is not a question but an appointment. When God calls us to His work, He has already equipped us before we ever began to question.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "Who am I?" Moses sees only his own smallness—a shepherd in the desert, no authority, no power. But the right question is not "Who am I?" but "Who is with me?" The Lord's presence, not our resume, is what qualifies us for His work.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "Certainly I will be with you." God does not promise that the task will be easy or that Moses will be eloquent; He promises His company. This is the deepest comfort: not exemption from hardship, but the certainty that we walk it with the God who loves us.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Moses asks for God's name before he goes—a wise man's request. If the enslaved people ask who sent him, Moses needs to speak truth with authority. Knowing the name of the God who calls us gives us courage to speak His word.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "I AM WHO I AM"—the revelation of God's self-existence, His self-sufficiency, His being that needs no source. In this name Moses hears that the God who sent him is not a local deity or a tribal god, but the ground of all existence itself.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: God binds His name to the memory of His people forever—"This is my name...my memorial to all generations." He commits Himself to be remembered, to be called upon. In an age when so many gods are forgotten, the living God writes His name into the hearts of His people.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "I have surely visited you"—the Lord speaks to the elders first, recalling His care and attention across the generations of exile. Before the mighty works, before the plagues, comes the word of His faithful seeing. He has been watching all along.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The promised land is described in the language of abundance and belonging—milk and honey, a place to dwell in peace. Redemption is not just freedom from slavery; it is inheritance of a home where the Lord has promised to meet His people.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "They will listen to your voice"—God grants Moses a word of encouragement. The elders will believe; the people will hear. When the Lord sends us, He prepares both the messenger and the listeners. Trust His ordering.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "The king of Egypt won't give you permission." God speaks truth plainly—this will not be easy negotiation. Pharaoh will resist. Yet the Lord announces hardship not to discourage Moses, but to prepare him, so he will not mistake resistance for failure.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Lord will strike Egypt with His wonders—His own hand, not Moses' eloquence, will break Pharaoh's will. We are not saved by persuasion, but by the power of God. When human strength fails, His reaches out to accomplish what only He can do.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "Favor in the sight of the Egyptians"—God will soften hearts even among the oppressors, so that Israel leaves not as fugitives but as a people honored and laden with gifts. His power extends even to turning the hearts of enemies.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Readers today hear an echo in this account of spoiling the Egyptians: God cares about the dignity and material welfare of His people, not just their souls. Even in redemption, He restores what was taken and honors those He rescues with genuine abundance and wholeness.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
